output.brief: The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not to the new installers or firmware 4.2. Brenmoor's lab matched claims to valve source, installer and firmware. Pellacott valves fail at about 41 per 1,000 in every installer and firmware group. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7. Warehouse valves that were never installed also leak: 11% of Pellacott 2026 valves, against 0% for Durrant-Hale. The calibration contractor found Pellacott's leak-test rig out of service since January, with no VA-220 test program on the other rigs. 31 of 36 certificates reuse four recycled value sequences, some already used in November 2025. The certificates, which lifted the SupplierPath score and earned dock-to-stock, therefore don't record real tests. I'm quite sure of this. What I can't tell yet is whether the Corlin seal or the new Line 3 is the physical cause, because every 2026 sample has both. Next steps: quarantine the 2026 Pellacott stock, including the six held lots. Do not release them on new certificates. Suspend dock-to-stock for Pellacott. Retest with Brenmoor's own helium test. Keep Durrant-Hale supplying. Require Pellacott to run a root-cause investigation on the seal and the line. Check the other suppliers' test records, since the programme rewarded paperwork. Drop the installer remediation plan.
